name: CHAOS-3465 Go parity: surplus retry leaves the budget episode alone + the half-cleared episode
$determination: CHAOS-3465 changed Python UNIT ADMISSION (sync/budget_guard.py's surplus phase, sync/guard.py's slot_headroom, the sync_units.py wiring). Go owns no unit-admission decision: internal/scheduler/sync mirrors Python's PLANNER (windows + HEAVY ratchet, pinned by planner_oracle_test.go, whose case schema carries no budget, deferral or concurrency field), and the only budget references in non-test Go source remain the two SQL episode clears at internal/providersync/repository_postgres.go:395-396 and internal/syncreconciler/lease_repair.go:383-384. _budget_deferral_exhausted -- the one Go-facing budget surface this repository pins -- is byte-identical across 7063b83ad. So the mirror is NO Go behaviour change. What it is instead: a probe that stops CHAOS-3465's two new Python writers of the shared sync_run_units row from invalidating the exhaustion corpus unobserved, and the two half-cleared-episode cases the corpus was missing. This file is the proof that both actually measure something.
$limitation: M1-M3 mutate LIVE PYTHON that the Go oracle executes at test time, so every proof below must run through `go test -count=1` with the live-oracle env set -- a cached PASS would report a killed mutation that was never run. M4 mutates the Go mirror. Not covered here, and covered elsewhere: the surplus phase's own behaviour (tests/test_chaos_3465_budget_surplus_retry.py, which carries its own mutation record in that PR), and the reached-state proofs against real PostgreSQL (internal/providersync/budget_episode_integration_test.go, internal/syncreconciler/lease_repair_integration_test.go, both integration-tagged).

mutations.rationale: The defect the probe exists for. A surplus promotion that restamps budget_first_deferred_at resets the episode's wall clock every time spare budget appears, so a unit that can never fit is rescued past CHAOS-3412's cap forever. Every authored case in the pair keeps passing -- none is built from the laundered state -- so without the probe this is invisible to the differential.

The other half of the same clause, on the WITHDRAWAL path rather than the promotion, and the one budget_guard's own comment calls out: _budget_deferral_exhausted's defence-in-depth gate reads result.error_category, so a surplus write that clears it disarms the exhaustion path for that unit. Mutating only the promotion (M1) would leave this path unmeasured -- the probe names both functions for exactly this reason.

A probe with nothing to check must fail, not pass. This is the vacuity mode the probe would otherwise acquire the day a surplus function is renamed and the tuple is 'fixed' by emptying it: the oracle would stay green while measuring nothing. Killed by the explicit empty-tuple refusal, not by any case.

Clause 1 of the Go mirror, mutated at the CONJUNCT rather than the whole condition. A half-cleared row (counter zeroed, stamp surviving) now short-circuits to 'not exhausted' in Go while live Python still terminalizes it. Recorded because it SURVIVED the pre-existing corpus: every zero-counter case there pairs the zero with a nil stamp, so the conjunct was never load-bearing for any of them. The two half_cleared_* cases added in this change are what kill it, and are the reason they are not decoration.
